title: Machine Learning Lab
tagline: Train your very own AI model
objectives: Understand how machines learn from examples
Train a model and watch its accuracy grow
Tell supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning apart
See why data quality decides how smart a model becomes
Sort training data from testing data

stages.title: Become an AI Trainer!
stages.narration: Machines don't follow hand written rules. They learn from examples, just like you. Today, you'll train one yourself!

steps.text: You show the model lots of labeled photos.
It hunts for patterns hidden in the examples.
With every example, it gets a little smarter.
Then it predicts things it has never seen before.

stages.title: Train Your First Model
stages.prompt: Feed labeled photos to the model one by one. Watch the accuracy bar climb as it learns the pattern!

test.prompt: A brand new photo arrives. What will YOUR model predict?

stages.explain: More labeled examples mean a smarter model. Notice the accuracy jumps fast at first, then slows down as it nears the top.

stages.title: Which Way Did It Learn?
stages.prompt: Every example below uses a different style of learning. Pick the right one for each.

tasks.label: Learning from emails labeled 'spam' or 'safe'
tasks.explain: Labeled answers are given, so this is supervised learning.

tasks.label: Grouping shoppers by habits, with no labels given
tasks.explain: No labels, just finding hidden groups. That's unsupervised learning.

tasks.label: A robot earning points for winning a game
tasks.explain: Learning by reward and trial is reinforcement learning.

tasks.label: Sorting photos already tagged 'cat' or 'dog'
tasks.explain: The tags are labels, so the model learns with supervision.

tasks.label: Bundling similar songs with no genre labels
tasks.explain: It discovers clusters on its own, with no labels to copy.

stages.title: Garbage In, Garbage Out
stages.prompt: Some training cards are mislabeled and will confuse the model. Tap the bad ones to toss them out, and keep the good ones. Watch the accuracy meter react!
stages.note: Clean, correctly labeled data is the secret to a smart model. Feed it junk, and it learns junk.
stages.explain: When you removed every wrong label and kept the good ones, accuracy hit 100%. Quality data beats lots of data.

stages.title: Training Data vs Testing Data
stages.prompt: A model studies with training data, then we check it with fresh testing data it has never seen. Sort each card.
stages.note: We always test on new, unseen data. Otherwise the model could just memorize the answers instead of truly learning.

cards.label: New photos the model never saw
Examples shown again and again to learn
A surprise quiz to check real skill

stages.title: Trainer's Final Test
stages.prompt: Score at least 80% to earn your Model Trainer badge.

questions.q: How does a machine learning model learn?
questions.explain: ML finds patterns in example data instead of following fixed rules.

questions.q: What usually makes a model more accurate?
questions.explain: More high quality labeled data helps the model learn better.

questions.q: Learning from data that has labels is called...
questions.explain: Labels act like an answer key, so it's supervised learning.

questions.q: Why do we test on new, unseen data?
questions.explain: Fresh data proves the model learned the pattern, not just memorized.

questions.q: What happens if you train on bad, messy data?
questions.explain: Garbage in, garbage out. Bad data leads to a bad model.

questions.q: Finding hidden groups with no labels is...
questions.explain: With no labels, the model groups data on its own. That's unsupervised.

questions.q: A robot that learns by earning rewards is using...
questions.explain: Reward based trial and error is reinforcement learning.

questions.q: What is a 'label' in training data?
options: The correct answer for an example
questions.explain: A label tells the model the right answer for that example.

stages.title: Lab Complete!
messages: 🏆 You earned the Model Trainer Badge
You trained a model and reached 98% accuracy
